counterevidence_considered.description: The discrete level assignment exists in the workflow as a potential source of the issue, but it is never routed to the exposure position.

evidence.description: The task authorizes the continuous prediction of the direct calibration fitted against the anchor measurement as the exposure.

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named workflow to the complete staged row sequence. The quantity that enters the association model's exposure position must be the continuous prediction of the direct calibration fitted against the supplied anchor measurement. A quantity confined to the finite set of level values does not satisfy this task.

evidence.description: The workflow assigns exactly that quantity to the exposure position: `reading` is the RidgeCV prediction from the direct fit against `anchor`, a continuous quantity, and it supplies `exposure`.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to demonstrate the issue by checking whether `reading` could be confined to the finite level set or could secretly be the label: RidgeCV regression predictions against the continuous anchor are continuous-valued and unrelated to the sorter's argmax output, and `exposure = reading` bypasses `label` entirely. I also considered whether 'direct calibration' might instead mean the pipelined `stack`/`wrapped` fit, but even under that alternative reading the exposure used is continuous, not a level assignment, so the in-scope issue class still would not be demonstrated. The attempt failed; the exposure conforms to an authorized continuous quantity.
